topics.title: Citizenship skills

outcomes.text: Form hypotheses, build reasoned arguments and reach substantiated conclusions about citizenship issues.
Formulate and sequence research questions to analyse citizenship issues and debates.
Select and organise knowledge to argue, counter opposing views and justify conclusions.
Describe methods governments, groups and individuals use to address issues, including practical action.
Present own and others' viewpoints on citizenship issues.
Plan practical citizenship actions that benefit others.
Evaluate how effective citizenship actions were.
Connect and compare citizenship concepts from local to global situations.

topics.title: 3.2.1 What are the principles and values that underpin British society?

outcomes.text: Study the make-up, values and dynamics of UK society, identity, media and the UK's world role.
State the key principles and values underpinning British society.
Explain citizens' human, moral, legal and political rights, duties, equalities and freedoms.
Identify factors that create individual, group, national and global identities.

topics.title: 3.2.2 What do we mean by identity?

outcomes.text: Explain how the four UK nations affect identity debates.
Describe population movement over time and the impact of immigration and migration on communities.
Explain why mutual respect is needed in a diverse society.
Describe multiple identities and the diverse UK population.

topics.title: 3.2.3 What is the role of the media and the free press?

outcomes.text: Explain the role of a free press in informing opinion, hosting debate and holding power to account.
Explain the media's right to report in the public interest, balanced by accuracy and privacy.
Describe press regulation and examples of censorship.

topics.title: 3.2.4 What is the UK's role in key international organisations?

outcomes.text: Describe the UK's relationships with the UN, NATO, EU, Council of Europe, Commonwealth and WTO.
Explain ongoing implications of leaving the EU.
Describe how the UK helps resolve international conflicts.
Explain how NGOs respond to humanitarian crises.

topics.title: 3.2.5 How can citizens make their voice heard and make a difference in society?

outcomes.text: Identify opportunities and barriers to participation in democracy.
Weigh the pros and cons of ways to hold power to account, such as campaigning, lobbying, petitions and demonstrations.
Explain how interest groups, pressure groups, unions and charities give people a voice.
Give two examples of citizens acting together to change their communities.
Explain how campaigners use the media.

topics.title: 3.2.6 Citizenship skills, processes and methods

outcomes.text: Use the key questions to set hypotheses and develop citizenship skills, often through case studies.

topics.title: 3.3.1 What laws does a society require and why?

outcomes.text: Study laws, the justice system, human rights and how citizens change the legal system.
Explain the principles of law: rights, presumption of innocence and equality before the law.
Explain how laws address fairness, justice and discrimination.
Balance rights and responsibilities in conflict situations from local to global.

topics.title: 3.3.2 What are a citizen's rights and responsibilities within the legal system?

outcomes.text: Describe the roles and powers of police, judiciary and legal representatives.
Explain how criminal and civil courts, tribunals and dispute resolution work.
State legal ages, including criminal responsibility, driving, marrying, voting and joining the forces.
Distinguish civil law from criminal law.
Compare the legal systems of England and Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland.

topics.title: 3.3.3 How has the law developed over time, and how does the law protect the citizen and deal with criminals?

outcomes.text: Trace how rights developed from Magna Carta to the Human Rights Act.
Distinguish common law from legislation.
Explain the right to representation, trade unions and employers' associations.
Describe types of crime, the profile of crime in the UK and factors affecting crime rates.
Describe strategies to reduce crime.
Describe forms of punishment, the purposes of sentencing and how effective sentences are.
Explain how the youth justice system works.

topics.title: 3.3.4 What are the universal human rights and how do we protect them?

outcomes.text: Explain the UN Universal Declaration, European Convention, Convention on the Rights of the Child and Human Rights Act.
Explain how international humanitarian law protects victims and sets rules of war.

topics.title: 3.3.5 How do citizens play a part to bring about change in the legal system?

outcomes.text: Describe citizen roles in the legal system: juror, witness, victim, magistrate, special constable and others.
Explain how groups and institutions campaign for legal change or against injustice.
Describe actions citizens take on human rights and justice, such as lobbying and petitions.

topics.title: 3.3.6 Citizenship processes, skills and methods

outcomes.text: Use the key questions to set hypotheses and develop citizenship skills, often through case studies.

topics.title: 3.4.1 Where does political power reside in the UK and how is it controlled?

outcomes.text: Study political power, democracy, government levels, parties, elections and political change.
Explain democracy, including representative democracy, and its underpinning values.
Describe the institutions of the British constitution and their powers.
Explain how the uncodified constitution works and how it is changing.

topics.title: 3.4.2 What are the powers of local and devolved government and how can citizens participate?

outcomes.text: Describe elected local government, its services and councillors' accountability.
Describe devolved government in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland and how powers are shared with Westminster.
Discuss the English votes for English laws debate.
Explain who can stand for election and how candidates are selected.
Explain who can vote, and debates about the voting age.
Discuss voter turnout, apathy and ways to raise participation.
Explain how taxes are raised and spent locally and nationally.
Explain budgeting and managing risk in public funding.
Compare viewpoints on welfare, health, elderly care and education provision.

topics.title: 3.4.3 Where does political power reside: with the citizen, parliament or government?

outcomes.text: Explain First Past the Post and how often Westminster elections happen.
Compare proportional and other voting systems used in the UK.
Distinguish the executive, legislature, judiciary and monarchy.
Explain the roles of the Commons, Lords and monarch in a bicameral parliament.
Describe how parliament scrutinises government through questions, committees and debates.
Describe the role of MPs and key parliamentary roles such as Speaker, whips and Black Rod.
Describe the legislative process.
Name major UK parties and their philosophical differences.
Explain how a government is formed by a majority or coalition.
Explain the role and power of the Prime Minister, cabinet and ministers.
Describe government departments, agencies and the civil service.

topics.title: 3.4.4 How do others govern themselves?

outcomes.text: Compare citizen participation in one democratic and one non-democratic system outside the UK.

topics.title: 3.4.5 How can citizens try to bring about political change?

outcomes.text: Explain how citizens contribute to parliamentary democracy and hold power to account.
Explain how digital democracy and social media may improve participation.
Describe actions citizens take, such as joining parties, campaigning, lobbying and demonstrating.
Explain how institutions, pressure groups, unions and charities give people a voice.

topics.title: 3.4.6 Citizenship skills, processes and methods

outcomes.text: Use the key questions to set hypotheses and develop citizenship skills, often through case studies.

topics.title: 3.5.1 Citizenship action - the actions of others

outcomes.text: Learn how citizens try to make a difference through case studies and your own action.
Analyse a citizenship action scenario using the fifth key question of each theme.

topics.title: 3.5.2 The investigation: taking citizenship action

outcomes.text: Choose a contemporary issue from the content and form an enquiry question.
Research the issue with primary and secondary sources and plan the action.
Take informed action such as letters, petitions or volunteering, and evaluate its effectiveness.
